ModuleName: 12 - Dynamic Objects and Controls with JavaScript and the DOM

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Outlines the module's core topics—including DOM structure, dynamic element creation and insertion, attribute and style modification, event handling, and JavaScript-driven UI controls—serving as a syllabus reference for learners and instructors to understand what concepts will be taught and in what sequence.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: Outlines the topics covered in the module, including the Document Object Model's structure, how JavaScript interacts with HTML elements at runtime, and dynamic manipulation of objects and controls; used by learners and instructors to preview and navigate the module's subject matter.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to the DOM and Dynamic Manipulation
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains what the DOM is, how browsers parse HTML into an in-memory tree structure, and how JavaScript can access and manipulate that tree at runtime, serving as the conceptual foundation learners need before writing any dynamic code.

Artifacts.Name: Creating and Inserting HTML Elements Dynamically
Artifacts.Description: A reading that covers how to use JavaScript methods such as createElement, appendChild, and insertBefore to generate new HTML elements on the fly and place them precisely within the document, teaching learners to build page content dynamically rather than relying on static markup.

Artifacts.Name: Modifying Existing Elements and Their Properties
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains how to select existing DOM elements and change their text content, HTML, attributes, CSS styles, and class lists using JavaScript without reloading the page, teaching learners to update a live interface in response to data or user actions.

Artifacts.Name: Adding and Managing Event Listeners
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains how browser events work and how to use addEventListener and removeEventListener to attach, manage, and respond to user interactions such as clicks, keystrokes, and form submissions, teaching learners to write structured, event-driven JavaScript.

Artifacts.Name: Building Interactive UI Controls with JavaScript
Artifacts.Description: A reading that walks through building fully hand-coded interactive UI controls — such as tabs, modals, or accordions — using only JavaScript to manage elements, events, and state transitions, giving learners practical experience constructing real front-end components without frameworks.

Artifacts.Name: Building Interactive UI Controls with JavaScript
